author: Codex assessment agent /root/libertarian_historical (AI-assisted)
changeNote: Completed each of the 240 current questions as an interpreted representative doctrine, with question-specific reasoning, source references and explicit conditional neutral modelling. Separate review pending. No 12Axes answer or score imported.

metadata.name: Civic nationalism (Scottish SNP tradition)
metadata.description: The contemporary Scottish SNP variant of civic nationalism: residence-based national belonging, democratic self-determination, European cooperation and a social-democratic programme. This is not every civic nationalist tradition.
metadata.scope: The SNP’s civic and social-democratic Scottish national project, anchored in its 2026 manifesto and checked against the Scottish Government’s 2026–27 budget and independent research on national identity. Scotland means the proposed self-governing nation in national questions; regions means its local territories except the explicitly applicable secession principle. Government delivery is evidence of this variant, not the definition of all civic nationalism. Manifesto intentions and budget allocations are distinguished from completed delivery; the cited budget is evidence of government spending plans, not proof that every allocation has been spent. New technologies and empirical causal questions use explicitly qualified representative modelling where the programme permits competing judgements; this is not a claimed completed questionnaire by the SNP.
metadata.phrase: A self-governing Scottish nation open to residents of different origins, combining shared citizenship with social protection and cooperation in Europe.

sources.title: Young SNP members: socio-nationalism, identity and politics

axes.brief: Popular self-determination and accountable parliamentary government define the selected civic variant. Specific recall devices are institutional inferences, not manifesto promises.
axes.counterEvidence: The SNP’s referendum mandate claim remains contested constitutionally. A democratic national project does not eliminate constitutional limits or guarantee agreement among all residents.

answers.rationale: The programme seeks electoral mandates and an independence referendum, making renewable popular authority central.
A panel of specialists would replace the equal civic participation underpinning the national project.
Residence-based equal political belonging is inconsistent with intelligence-based voting qualifications.
Parliamentary self-government entails legislation through accountable institutions rather than unilateral executive override.
Democratic self-determination requires opponents to compete under equal rules, including opponents of independence.
Public-service spending commitments require parliamentary scrutiny by representatives outside the executive.
The manifesto’s human-rights incorporation supports judicial checks against unlawful government decisions.
Trade unions are partners in this social-democratic programme, not a privileged replacement electorate.
The leadership’s preferred constitutional outcome does not justify excluding peaceful opposing parties.
Referendums are accepted mechanisms for binding popular decisions, though every repeal would need lawful procedures.
A sovereign people acts through accountable institutions rather than surrendering all policy to one leader.
Constitutional removal for serious abuse follows the programme’s democratic accountability commitments.
Electoral legitimacy would be undermined by a leader deciding alone to delay renewed consent.
A defined recall process is compatible with citizen control, inferred without claiming a specific SNP recall pledge.
Government without electoral or parliamentary accountability contradicts the programme’s rationale for self-government.
Military substitution for an elected civilian government contradicts the democratic state envisaged.

axes.brief: Rights, rehabilitation and inclusion coexist with a funded national police service and public-health intervention.
axes.counterEvidence: The programme proposes stronger police powers against antisocial activity, certain content prohibitions and protection of vulnerable groups. It is not a maximal-liberty or minimal-policing doctrine.

answers.rationale: The public-health and recovery approach to drugs favours less punitive personal-use policy, qualified by safeguards against harm.
A serious-crime investigation under judicial authorisation fits the programme’s combination of safety and rights.
Democratic participation supports peaceful protest with emergency access, subject to proportionate access safeguards.
The proposed anti-SLAPP law specifically protects public criticism and campaigning from intimidation.
Public-health prevention supports protective measures while the rights programme resists unlimited paternalism; neither a blanket power nor absolute prohibition follows.
The privacy implications of indiscriminate long-term movement records outweigh a general safety rationale without individual suspicion.
Road-safety enforcement supports proportionate intoxication testing, although the exact random-testing procedure is inferred.
Preventing credible violence through a court-supervised order fits the emphasis on protection and due process.
Adult access is generally protected, but the programme restricts abusive sexual material; mere moral disapproval is insufficient.
Digital inclusion and civil liberty favour ordinary access without government identification for every user.
An exceptional violence risk and individual search safeguards pull in opposite directions; the programme does not license a blanket suspicionless regime.
Credible serious disorder can justify proportionate public-order restrictions, while peaceful disagreement remains protected.
Judicially supervised home searches fit equal access to justice and protection from arbitrary intrusion.
Public-interest disclosure is supported by accountable government and anti-SLAPP principles, qualified by genuine safety needs.
The programme’s collective safety and violence-prevention approach does not treat personal-defence firearms as an ordinary general entitlement.
Indefinite detention without independent court review conflicts with the stated human-rights framework.

axes.brief: Belonging is based on living in and contributing to Scotland; Scottish languages and heritage remain valued within plural membership.
axes.counterEvidence: NatCen finds residents’ actual identities mix civic and ethnic elements. Breniaux’s youth-member research describes a socio-political variant; neither establishes that all Scots are uniformly multicultural.

answers.rationale: Residence-based belonging resists automatic priority for established customs over migrants’ identities.
Inclusive public services support reasonable cultural accommodation, with practical budget constraints.
Joining the nation need not mean adopting every inherited Scottish custom.
The civic account explicitly makes belonging available across origin and identity.
Shared communication matters, but recognition of Gaelic, Scots and diverse residents prevents a simple single-language priority.
Acknowledging longstanding communities fits inclusive public recognition, inferred rather than claiming an Indigenous Scottish policy equivalent.
Support for Scottish heritage coexists with inclusive cultural participation; neither exclusive predominant funding nor indifference follows.
The project needs a shared civic community, so distinct identities do not automatically outrank common civic commitments.
A plural public community can accommodate celebrations rather than insist on one cultural calendar.
The national community is described through the people who live there, allowing multiple traditions.
Participation in shared civic institutions is encouraged without requiring cultural erasure.
Accessible services for migrant residents support proportionate local multilingual signage.
Shared citizenship and continued community attachments are compatible; families need not rank one identity universally above another.
Religious inclusion favours dress freedom, but the proposed exemption from otherwise applicable covering rules requires an equality and safety judgement.
Multiple cultural ways of life fit a residence-based Scottish national identity.
Integration should build civic participation rather than replace migrants’ distinct customs with national ones.

axes.brief: The 2026 programme calls for a Scottish visa, workers and students, and a welcoming refugee policy.
axes.counterEvidence: Recruitment targets specific economic sectors, and an immigration system still exists. Welcoming migration is not an unconditional promise that every unauthorised arrival remains permanently.

answers.rationale: An inflexible annual ceiling conflicts with the programme’s aim to attract people for changing demographic and economic needs.
Welcoming residents seeking work and a better life supports general settlement opportunities.
Workers are sought, but refugees and community membership are not reduced to a preferred-skills test.
Inclusive settlement and refugee belonging favour family unity, inferred from the programme rather than a specific numerical pledge.
The refugee section affirms belonging and humanitarian protection without making skills or cultural similarity preconditions.
Opposition to harsh enforcement supports humane regularisation, but does not establish unconditional residence for every immigration-law violation.
The proposed Scottish visa is intended to meet employers’ and communities’ needs for more workers.
Housing investment and migration are treated as compatible priorities rather than migration reduction being the default remedy.
Family unity should not simply inherit a rigid general cap inconsistent with the inclusive migration approach.
The manifesto expressly seeks people wanting to work in Scottish businesses, universities and public services.
Employer routes can facilitate entry, but humanitarian and other settlement grounds should not all require a sponsor.
The programme welcomes international university talent and criticises restrictions that harm universities, supporting routes for graduates.
Humanitarian protection is presented as a commitment distinct from ordinary economic migration planning.
A nation defined by residence and participation should not rank applicants by cultural resemblance.
Inclusive services and assistance to people without recourse to public funds support access subject to ordinary need and eligibility rules.
The refugee section positively values newcomers’ contributions to society and culture, while not making difference the sole admissions test.

axes.brief: Conventional defence and support for Ukraine coexist with opposition to nuclear weapons and a peace-oriented foreign policy.
axes.counterEvidence: The manifesto seeks stronger conventional defence and defence-sector investment. Anti-nuclear policy therefore cannot be scored as pacifism at any cost.

answers.rationale: National advantage alone is insufficient for force under the programme’s peace, international law and sovereignty commitments.
Peace, diplomacy and a negotiated two-state settlement exemplify preference for political solutions.
Stronger conventional defence is supported, but indefinite spending for superiority is balanced against public-service priorities.
A clearly imminent attack can justify defensive action within the stated rule-of-law framework.
Defence against aggression is the normal justification, though an imminent threat need not be allowed to strike first.
The civilian democratic programme favours capable conventional forces without proposing compulsory male service.
Diplomatic concessions may prevent conflict, qualified by the programme’s refusal to abandon Ukraine’s sovereignty.
Autonomous lethal targeting without human approval sits uneasily with the stated human-rights and accountable defence approach.
Conventional defence is justified by keeping Scotland safe rather than an expansionist military mission.

The programme explicitly supports capable conventional armed forces for protection. This contradicts a rule against all military action at any cost; its solidarity with Ukraine is not by itself proof of a promise to enter that war.
Credible defence can require deployable forces, but the programme does not make prolonged overseas campaigning an objective in itself.
Peace and international law favour leaving a dispute unsettled over launching a war to seize territory.
Deterrence may protect sovereignty, while threats for concessions can undermine the peace-oriented approach; the case matters.
Avoiding unnecessary war usually outweighs displays of resolve, without sacrificing collective defence.
Necessary defensive intelligence can be justified, but avoidable escalation for a vague advantage is not endorsed automatically.
Opposition to nuclear armaments supports negotiated reductions in dangerous capabilities.

axes.brief: Scottish independence is paired with EU membership, international rights and shared responses to climate and humanitarian problems.
axes.counterEvidence: Self-determination is not rejection of all shared authority. EU membership, withdrawal rights and the independence objective create deliberately mixed answers across sovereignty items.

answers.rationale: Scottish democratic authority matters, but voluntary EU membership entails binding shared law in agreed fields.
The commitment to rejoin the EU accepts binding joint decisions, bounded by treaties and democratic consent.
Human-rights incorporation and EU membership weigh against unconditional final domestic judicial supremacy.
Security and European partnerships justify durable commitments that can constrain unilateral action.
Self-determination supports a lawful exit route from political commitments without an international institution’s discretionary veto.
Rule-of-law internationalism supports binding adjudication, subject to legitimate treaty jurisdiction.
Climate justice and human rights can justify commitments beyond immediate national advantage.
The programme treats the climate emergency as a shared international responsibility requiring coordinated authority.
EU re-entry rejects remaining outside all blocs with coordinated foreign policy obligations.
The manifesto proposes incorporating international human-rights conventions into domestic law.
Economic self-government and European cooperation are both valued; neither a permanent national currency monopoly nor immediate shared monetary authority follows here.
International development and climate funds demonstrate support for shared finance and problem-solving.
EU membership and a welcoming migration approach qualify claims to wholly unilateral border authority.
Single-market access explicitly depends on common trade rules rather than unilateral national regulation alone.
Independent statehood is the stated objective; joining the EU is not presented as immediate absorption into a single political federation.
Support for Ukraine and global rights entails upholding agreed rules beyond a narrowly neutral immediate interest.

axes.brief: A mixed economy combines private enterprise with public NHS, water, rail and strategic investment.
axes.counterEvidence: Business growth and inward investment are explicit aims; public-service ownership does not imply nationalising most ordinary firms.

answers.rationale: The programme encourages commercial businesses to start and grow within a mixed economy.
It explicitly commits to keeping Scottish Water publicly owned.
Comparable outcomes leave accountability and strategic purpose relevant; there is no universal private-title preference.
Public investment and strategic enterprises are legitimate where they serve development, without replacing every competitor.
The strong public NHS model weighs against a general preference for privately owned healthcare facilities.

Publicly owned rail services and investment in railway connections support a qualified inference in favour of public infrastructure. ScotRail operating ownership is distinct from ownership of tracks; the source does not announce an infrastructure takeover.
Efficiency matters, but public accountability and service integration also matter when choosing contracting arrangements.
The developmental public-investment model supports a public financial institution alongside commercial finance.
A blanket sale rule conflicts with retained public transport and water commitments.

The manifesto’s social-rent programme includes local authorities as well as registered social landlords and pension investors. It supports a substantial public role, but publicly financed affordable housing is not necessarily publicly owned housing.
The defence sector includes private firms, but strategic public control may also be justified; ownership depends on the asset.
Taking energy benefits into Scottish hands combines public strategic control and private investment rather than requiring universal public extraction.
Councils may compare their own operation with contracting; neither mode is made categorically superior.
Strategic transport and utility ownership is valued beyond short-term receipts from asset sales.
Persistent losses warrant reform, but social necessity can justify subsidy; sale is not automatic.
A common civic public sphere supports public-service broadcasting alongside independent media.

axes.brief: The selected civic nationalism seeks EU single-market access and international investment, while retaining worker, climate and strategic safeguards.
axes.counterEvidence: Support for local supply chains and defence production qualifies an otherwise open-trade orientation.

answers.rationale: Single-market re-entry favours reducing general tariffs rather than routine shelter for domestic businesses.
EU access is promoted for growth despite competitive pressures on particular firms.
Local jobs and supply chains matter, but lower-cost procurement and common trade obligations also count.
Businesses benefit from international supply chains subject to ordinary security and standards rules.
Resilience of essential supply is valued alongside access to European suppliers, requiring sector-specific judgement.
Openness is favoured, but negotiating common reciprocal rules is preferred over prescribing every unilateral reduction.
Industrial support is accepted, yet blanket import restrictions can conflict with single-market rules.
The investment programme actively seeks foreign investors, with fair standards applying to them.
Agricultural resilience is important but does not imply general exclusion of imported food.
Competitive business growth within the single market is preferred to routine trade protection.
Rules-based remedies can respond to discrimination, but tariff retaliation is not inherently desirable.
Common-market participation favours nondiscriminatory product taxation under shared rules.
Subsidised imports raise fairness issues, but proportionate shared trade remedies rather than blanket bans are appropriate.
EU market integration accepts greater trade interdependence alongside resilience planning.
Strategic security can warrant scrutiny, while the programme strongly welcomes external investment.
International digital trade supports growth unless specific safety, privacy or security rules justify limits.

axes.brief: Business initiative works within public investment, fair-work rules, climate strategy and selected price interventions.
axes.counterEvidence: The manifesto proposes reducing bureaucracy and enabling firms, not comprehensive compulsory production planning.

answers.rationale: Ordinary businesses are encouraged to grow and choose products rather than obey detailed output commands.
The growth council and project coordination do not amount to compulsory production quotas across key industries.
Most commercial prices remain market-based within consumer and competition protections.
Strategic projects and sector investment are explicitly directed toward national development priorities.
Commercial growth is encouraged through customer demand, though socially necessary services may receive support.
The programme proposes action on essential supermarket prices and administered transport fares.
Reducing business bureaucracy supports entry without having to prove additional production is necessary.
Public investment may target priorities, but compelling every private bank’s lending is a stronger measure than the programme establishes.
Inward investment and European integration favour capital mobility subject to legitimate regulation.
Targeted growth support and green-sector investment deliberately influence economic development.
Innovation in finance and public monetary stability must be balanced; neither unregulated private currencies nor complete prohibition is required.
Fair work and protection of low-paid workers support a legal wage floor.
Collective bargaining within legal floors is preferred to universal government wage schedules.
Macroeconomic support for development is legitimate, but direct political control of every interest decision is not established.
Tenant protection and affordability measures qualify reliance on unregulated market rents.
A strategic mixed economy still leaves most production decisions to enterprises rather than comprehensive routine coordination.

axes.brief: Progressive taxation and child-poverty reduction are central; the 2026–27 budget funds substantial household support.
axes.counterEvidence: The manifesto also promises tax-band stability and growth, so equality goals do not imply limitless tax increases.

answers.rationale: Progressive taxation and income support explicitly aim to reduce poverty and unequal living standards.
Reducing unjustified material disparities is accepted as a reason for progressive taxation.
The child-payment and poverty agenda supports strengthening minimum household resources.
The programme seeks fuller social participation rather than a merely subsistence safety net.
It explicitly asks wealthier people to contribute a larger share through progressive taxation.
Tax retention is balanced against funding redistribution and public services, rather than prioritised despite inequality.
Wealth taxation and fair contribution principles support a qualified inheritance-tax-funded transfer inference.
Poverty reduction opposes an arbitrary cutoff that leaves otherwise eligible people without enough support.
The manifesto calls for exploring wealth taxation and expanding high-value property contributions.
Support levels are framed around need and inclusion rather than being kept modest principally for taxpayers.
Reducing the cost of disability and digital exclusion extends support beyond bare physical survival.
Eradicating child poverty gives income support priority over a general tax-cut-first rule.
Support to households on low earnings fits the programme’s cost-of-living and poverty commitments.
Progressive marginal taxation directly contradicts equal marginal rates at every income level.
The social-democratic land and community-development approach supports compensated redistribution where it broadens opportunity.
Working poverty and participation barriers justify assistance beyond only households unable to survive.

axes.brief: Equal citizenship and rights-based legislation support secular public authority with accommodation of voluntary religious identity.
axes.counterEvidence: Scottish religious traditions and denominational education complicate a strict exclusion of all religious expression from public life. The civic criterion is equal standing, not state atheism.

answers.rationale: A shared civic legal order must be justifiable to residents of different faiths and none.
No particular religious teaching is the controlling official source in this equal-citizenship programme.
Democratically accountable policy does not require clerical permission.
Constitutional religious preference conflicts with the residence-based national community, though heritage may be acknowledged.
Inclusive education favours understanding religions without a universal duty to cultivate one faith.
A compulsory national faith curriculum would conflict with inclusive belonging; voluntary denominational choices are separate.
Civil institutions and common human-rights rules should determine legally enforceable decisions.
An official religious veto would give unelected clergy a privileged position over equal citizens.
Optional multi-faith ceremonial participation may be inclusive, while compulsory worship would not be; a blanket exclusion is not required.
Public money may support community services, but strengthening belief as such is not a civic state’s objective.
Official endorsement of one faith should be avoided, while historical or educational displays may remain.
Inherited holidays can have civic convenience and cultural meaning without requiring official religious endorsement.
Religious office alone should not confer a governing seat under equal civic representation.
Comparable charitable activity should receive comparable treatment rather than extra privilege merely for religious identity.
Civil marriage should not depend on religious approval, consistent with equal LGBTQI+ rights.
Voluntary mediation can be respected, but binding family-law authority must preserve consent and civil equality.

axes.brief: The manifesto explicitly supports LGBTQI+ equality, reproductive healthcare, inclusive education and changing discriminatory institutions.
axes.counterEvidence: Public consultation and protection of rights still constrain implementation. Progressive reform does not mean every customary practice must disappear.

answers.rationale: The equality agenda supports changing customs that exclude people as public values evolve.
Longstanding practice is not given priority over equal rights and inclusion.
Family support and LGBTQI+ equality favour equal recognition beyond a single household model.
Equal opportunity and protection of diverse identities oppose prescribing distinct traditional roles.
Equal LGBTQI+ rights support marriage regardless of the partners’ sex.
Supporting children and families does not require socially privileging only one conventional household arrangement.
The programme’s reproductive-rights approach supports acceptance of early abortion as a personal healthcare choice.
The commitment to inclusive LGBTQI+ schooling limits a parental veto over factual inclusive education.
Equal treatment and family inclusion favour equal acceptance of same-sex adoptive parents.
Personal dignity and diverse identities are more important than enforcing inherited dress expectations.
The manifesto expressly commits to recognising and respecting trans people’s identities.
Inherited morals may be taught but should not outrank inclusion and the ability to challenge discrimination.
Equal rights support acceptance of adults pursuing roles regardless of conventional sex expectations.
Urgent equality changes need not await gradualism merely because an institution is longstanding.
The manifesto celebrates LGBTQI+ inclusive education and intends to continue it.
Heritage is valued, but voluntary preservation and critical reform coexist; ancestry alone is not a decisive reason either way.

axes.brief: The programme supports AI, investment and infrastructure alongside climate compatibility, nature restoration and precaution in health.
axes.counterEvidence: It rejects new nuclear stations and uses case-by-case climate tests for oil and gas, while accelerating major projects. Neither blanket technological enthusiasm nor blanket opposition fits.

answers.rationale: Growth and useful innovation are actively encouraged, with regulation rather than waiting for all uncertainty to vanish.
Trials help establish safety, but limiting every technology until long-term evidence is substantial would obstruct the growth agenda.
Faster infrastructure and habitat restoration are both commitments, requiring case-specific mitigation rather than automatic approval.
Public healthcare responsibilities support substantial safety evaluation before widespread medical deployment.
Productivity innovation is supported alongside retraining and a just transition for displaced workers.
Nature protection is important, but the major-projects programme does not make every untouched habitat an absolute veto.
Low-carbon food innovation could help, but agricultural livelihoods and ecological assessment also matter; the programme supplies no universal priority.
For healthy-person brain enhancement, uncertain long-term harm supports cautious trials as an analogy from healthcare safeguards.
Renewable technology and lower resource impacts are both used, rather than an exclusive technology-over-consumption strategy.
Climate compatibility and environmental assessment justify delay where important project harms remain unclear.
Adult choice supports access, while public-health safeguards question whether basic tests suffice for brain enhancement.

NHS accountability and equal patient protection support testing diagnostic reliability across groups before wide adoption. This applies to supervised as well as autonomous AI; the exact trial-only rule is an inference rather than a stated programme pledge.
Scientific opportunity competes with irreversible intergenerational risks; controlled enhancement trials require ethical safeguards beyond disease treatment.
Ecosystem restoration and precaution favour long-term ecological evidence before broad crop deployment.
Affordable housing and transport need expansion, but protecting nature remains an independent priority.
Irreversible serious harm warrants a higher evidence threshold despite promising early benefits.

axes.brief: Scottish self-determination and local empowerment coexist with strong Scotland-wide public services.
axes.counterEvidence: National policing, NHS planning and common equality standards are centralising elements within the desired Scottish state; independence is not a promise of universal municipal autonomy.

answers.rationale: The claim to Scottish self-government rejects a remote national executive’s unrestricted override of a region’s democratic authority.
Constitutionally protected competences should not be defined solely by the larger national government in a dispute.
A democratic referendum is the stated route to Scottish independence.
Local consent and protected devolution limit automatic override for a nationwide programme.
The project supports meaningful constitutional self-government within protected individual rights.
The manifesto funds and strengthens the unified Police Scotland model.
Local fiscal resources matter, but redistribution across Scotland also supports equal services in poorer areas.
A common national educational entitlement and inclusive curriculum justify shared requirements, while local delivery can vary.
Local taxation and council-tax reform recognise local fiscal powers within a common framework.
Common fair-work protections support national employment floors despite local preferences for weaker rules.
Community empowerment supports local institutional choice within fair constitutional procedures.
The NHS model supports common national treatment entitlements to reduce geographic inequality.
Territorial communities may govern local affairs with rights protections; this is an inclusive self-government analogy, not an invented Scottish Indigenous polity.
Local accountability and tax competition coexist with nationwide service equity, requiring limits proportionate to spillovers.
Local environmental decisions are appropriate where effects remain local and common protections are met.
Cross-regional emergencies justify coordinated national leadership with local expertise and oversight.

axes.brief: The programme emphasises education, poverty, trauma and inclusive institutions as influences on people, without asserting biological uniformity.
axes.counterEvidence: Civic equality does not establish scientific explanations of IQ, temperament or attention. Neutral responses preserve mixed empirical possibilities; they are disclosed modelling decisions, not empirical findings.

answers.rationale: Early support, education and poverty interventions assume substantial social shaping of conduct, supporting a moderate social emphasis.
The residence-based rejection of inherited national worth and emphasis on educational opportunity weigh against attributing national test gaps mainly to ancestry.
Equal opportunity and challenging gender expectations give socialisation a substantial explanatory role, without denying biology.
The programme combines mental-health care and trauma support; it does not rank biological susceptibility against experience universally.
Expanding opportunities and education treats interests as meaningfully shaped by what people experience and can access.
Safety policy addresses behaviour and context while permitting individual predispositions; inherited-versus-learned risk shares remain mixed.
Inclusive community institutions and early intervention treat cooperative habits as socially cultivable.
Trauma-informed support recognises experience without claiming empathy has no biological component or fixing the relative weight.
Educational and disability support attend both environmental barriers and individual capacities; neither is universally ranked above the other.
Inclusive education and changing discriminatory attitudes place substantial weight on learned moral expectations rather than fixed inherited reactions.
Trauma-informed justice and prevention treat experiences as important in shaping perceived threats.
Temperament can interact with upbringing; civic membership supplies no single physiological causal theory.
Recognition of different identities leaves both cultural ideals and individual embodied preferences possible without a fixed ranking.
The programme addresses violence through social prevention, trauma and institutions, rather than assigning racial groups inherited violence propensities.
Early intervention, education and rehabilitation treat self-control as developable rather than inherited through racial categories.
The programme’s attention to gender inequality, care and opportunity weighs against dismissing social expectations as a pay-gap cause; market value alone is not a biological explanation.

review.reviewer: Codex /root, separate evidence review of /root/libertarian_historical assessment
review.notes: Reviewed all 240 answers and axis briefs against the current literal questions. Independently read the SNP 2026 manifesto text, the Scottish Budget delivery chapter, NatCen identity findings and Breniaux research. Made the selected Scottish SNP variant explicit in the display name. Corrected rail-operations versus infrastructure ownership and public funding versus public housing title; moderated these ownership inferences. Clarified defence against an absolute no-war rule without claiming sanctuary for Ukrainians proves commitment to enter war. Corrected diagnostic-AI wording, which is not limited to autonomous systems. Added verified publication dates and clarified that budget allocations and manifesto proposals are not completed implementation. Reviewed neutral warnings in trade, technology and Culture/Nature; these are conditional representative judgements, not scientific estimates. Equal civic status alone is not evidence of a genetic causal theory. No values were adjusted to avoid similarity.

similarity.reason: Reviewed revision 1 of both profiles after independent literal-question and evidence checks. Retain both scoped subjects despite the diagnostic overlap: Scottish SNP civic nationalism centres national self-determination and residence-based membership, whereas US egalitarian liberal feminism centres gendered autonomy, equal political agency and reform of care institutions. The current questions capture much shared liberal and social-democratic policy, so similar coordinates do not establish doctrinal identity. Ownership, military, fiscal and secession responses retain evidence-based distinctions; source-supported values were not tuned to create distance. This decision is a named scope-retention judgement, not a claim that all civic nationalists or feminists share either profile.
